savings_or_continuation_provisions.quote: Nothing in this order shall be construed to impair or otherwise affect: (i) the authority granted by law to an executive department or agency, or the head thereof; or (ii) the functions of the Director of the Office of Management and Budget relating to budgetary, administrative, or legislative proposals.
savings_or_continuation_provisions.note: Standard no-impair clause. It protects statutory agency authority and OMB functions, not the provisions, offices or actions of the revoked orders, so it saves nothing of the five batch orders.

savings_or_continuation_provisions.quote: shall promptly consider taking steps to rescind any orders, rules, regulations, guidelines, or policies, or portions thereof, implementing or enforcing the Presidential actions identified in section 1 of this order, as appropriate and consistent with applicable law, including the Administrative Procedure Act
savings_or_continuation_provisions.note: Treats agency rules and policies already issued under a listed order as separate acts that stay until the agency rescinds them under the APA. It is a directive to consider rescission, not a savings clause: it preserves no provision, office or right of any revoked order.

effective_date_reading: Sec. 1 says 'The following Presidential actions are revoked' and no effective-date, delayed-effect or phase-in wording appears anywhere in the order (secs. 1-3 read in full). The revocations took effect on signing, February 24, 2021 (printed 86 FR 11855-11856, March 1, 2021).

targets_in_batch_05.EO:13772: sec. 1 ('Executive Order 13772 of February 3, 2017', first listed)

conclusion: EO 14018 (signed 2021-02-24, 86 FR 11855-11856, PDF pages 1-2, read once in full) revokes seven Presidential actions in sec. 1: five Executive orders (13772, 13828, 13924, 13967, 13979) and two Memoranda. Sec. 2 tells OMB and the agency heads to consider rescinding implementing orders, rules, regulations, guidelines and policies and says personnel positions, committees, task forces and other entities established under the listed actions 'shall be abolished, as appropriate and consistent with applicable law'. Sec. 3 is a no-impair clause for statutory agency authority and OMB functions plus implementation and no-private-rights wording. The order has no savings, pending-matter or exception clause, no effective-date wording, and no successor delegation or transfer of functions or funds. The two 'transfer' hits the machine counted are words in the title of a revoked Memorandum ('Delegation of Certain Authority Under the Federal Service Labor-Management Relations Statute'), not an operative transfer. The abolition wording in sec. 2 is the opposite of a transfer: it winds down entities the listed orders created.
